summary: Adds lag, overshoot, velocity limits, and acceleration limits to CHOP channels for smoothed control motion.
key_concepts: Adds lag and overshoot to channels and can also limit channel velocity and acceleration.
Separate up and down values allow fast-rise slow-fall behavior or the reverse.
Lag Method changes whether up/down means value direction, amplitude direction, vector magnitude, or quaternion rotation.
Lag time is approximately how long the output takes to follow 90 percent of an input change.
Snap forces output values back to the input when they are within Threshold.
Lag per Sample applies lag independently to each sample for multi-sample channels.

key_params.name: lagmethod
key_params.note: Apply lag by value, amplitude, magnitude, or quaternion rotation

key_params.name: lag
key_params.note: Separate lag values for rising and falling changes

key_params.name: lagunit
key_params.note: Samples, frames, or seconds for lag values

key_params.name: lagsamples
key_params.note: Apply lag per sample for multi-sample channels

key_params.name: snap
key_params.note: Snap output when input/output difference is below threshold

key_params.name: reset
key_params.note: Bypass lag and reset while on

common_gotchas: Lag up/down are independent; asymmetric values create fast-rise/slow-fall behavior that planners should make intentional.
Lag Magnitude treats channels as one vector, so only the first Lag/Overshoot/Clamp value applies.
Quaternion Rotation mode is a Commercial feature and should be selected only for quaternion rotation channels.
Lag introduces temporal memory; provide a reset path for reusable rigs or stateful scene changes.
For a less abrupt smoothing effect, official docs point to Filter CHOP.
